chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Two rak'ahs that the married man prays are superior to seventy rak'ahs that the unmarried man prays."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of a married man's prayer compared to an unmarried man's?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the status of marriage by linking it to spiritual reward, noting that just two units of prayer performed by a married man surpass seventy units by an unmarried man. This comparison underscores the theological significance of marital duties (*sunan al-nikah*) as a means of sanctifying daily life, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the family unit as a foundation for spiritual growth and social stability.
